title: Skilled Worker visa for the United Kingdom: a sponsored job in an eligible occupation, usually paying at least £41,700 a year and the going rate, with English at B2

sources.title: Immigration Rules, Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 1.3: the applicant must be aged 18 or over on the date of application
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 3.3: a person must not be applying for entry clearance as a Skilled Worker as a national or citizen of Afghanistan
Explanatory memorandum to Statement of Changes HC 1691, para. 5.3: Skilled Worker visa applications from main applicants who are nationals of Afghanistan are refused from 26 March 2026
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 5.1 to 5.3: a valid Certificate of Sponsorship for the job, from a sponsor authorised for the Skilled Worker route and listed as A-rated
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 4.2 and the table after SW 4.4, option A: a salary of at least £41,700 per year and the going rate for the SOC 2020 occupation code
Immigration Rules, Appendix Skilled Occupations, Tables 1 to 3: the eligible occupations, skilled to RQF level 6 or above, and their going rates
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 6.1: the job must be in an eligible SOC 2020 occupation code listed in Table 1, Table 2 or Table 3 of Appendix Skilled Occupations, or the Immigration Salary List
Appendix Skilled Worker, table after SW 4.4, options B and C: a relevant PhD with £37,500 and 90% of the going rate; a STEM PhD with £33,400 and 80% of the going rate
Appendix Skilled Worker, table after SW 4.4, options D and E: a job on the Immigration Salary List with £33,400 and the going rate; a new entrant with £33,400 and 70% of the going rate
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 4.1 and 7.1 to 7.2: English at CEFR level B2 in reading, writing, speaking and listening, shown as Appendix English Language specifies
Appendix English Language, EL 4.1, EL 5.1 and EL 6.1: a national of a majority-English-speaking country, an academic qualification taught in English, or an approved English language test
Explanatory memorandum to Statement of Changes HC 1333, paras. 5.22, 5.23 and 6.4: the Skilled Worker English requirement rises from B1 to B2 for first grants from 8 January 2026
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 15.2 and 15.3: from abroad, £1,270 held for a 28-day period, unless the A-rated sponsor certifies it will maintain and accommodate the applicant
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 26.3, 29.1, 29.1A, 29.2 and 32A.1 to 32A.2: a dependent partner aged 18 or over and dependent children of a Skilled Worker sponsored for a job in Table 1, 2 or 3
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 33.3 and 33.5: £285 for a dependent partner, £315 for the first dependent child, £200 for any other, held for a 28-day period
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 29.1A and 32A.2: a partner or child joins only a Skilled Worker sponsored for a job in Table 1, Table 2 or Table 3 of Appendix Skilled Occupations, save listed exceptions
Appendix Skilled Worker, SW 18.1: permission until 14 days after the end date of the certificate of sponsorship, which may be up to 5 years after its start date
Home Office immigration and nationality fees, 8 October 2026: Skilled Worker per person, £819 or £1,618 from outside the UK and £943 or £1,865 inside it, by certificate length
Pay for UK healthcare as part of your immigration application, how much you pay: £1,035 per year, or £776 per year for applicants under the age of 18 at the time of application
Appendix Relationship with Partner, RWP 1.1 and 5.1: both partners 18 or over; if not married or civil partners, a relationship similar to marriage for at least 2 years
Appendix Children, CHI 1.1, 1.2, 1A.1 and 3.2: under 18, or older after permission as a dependent child; no partner, living with a parent; both parents come unless one has sole responsibility
Immigration Rules, introduction, para. 5C and definitions: not for Irish citizens who need no leave; a partner is a spouse, civil or unmarried partner of 2 years; a parent is not a step-parent
Immigration Act 1971, s. 2(1)(a): a person has the right of abode in the United Kingdom if they are a British citizen
Immigration Act 1971, s. 3ZA(1): an Irish citizen does not require leave to enter or remain in the United Kingdom

requirements.title: Not a British or Irish citizen: they live and work in the UK without a visa
Not applying from abroad as a citizen of Afghanistan (refused since 26 March 2026); a dual national, or someone switching from another permission inside the UK: possible

assessments.title: A Certificate of Sponsorship from a licensed, A-rated employer for the job
A job in an eligible occupation in Table 1, 2 or 3 of Appendix Skilled Occupations, or a table the rules name for a particular case (such as 1a, 2aa or 3a), or on the Immigration Salary List
A salary of at least £41,700 a year and the going rate for the occupation (option A)
Or, with a PhD relevant to the job, £37,500 a year and 90% of the going rate; with a STEM PhD, £33,400 and 80% of the going rate
Or, for a job on the Immigration Salary List, £33,400 a year and the going rate; for a new entrant at the start of their career, £33,400 and 70% of the going rate
English at level B2 in reading, writing, speaking and listening (B1 if the last Skilled Worker permission required B1), shown in a way Appendix English Language allows
Savings of £1,270 held for 28 days by the worker, unless the A-rated sponsor certifies it will maintain and accommodate them
Plus £285 for a partner, £315 for the first child and £200 for each other child, held for 28 days, unless the sponsor certifies it will maintain them

dependents.title: Spouse aged 18 or over; only if the worker's job is in Table 1, 2 or 3 (not checked)
Partner aged 18 or over, after 2 years in a relationship similar to marriage; a shorter one, which may be a civil partnership: possible; job in Table 1, 2 or 3 (not checked)
Children under 18 with no spouse or partner; living with the principal and the other parent coming too are not checked; an adult child: possible; job in Table 1, 2 or 3 (not checked)

costs.title: Visa fee from outside the UK, certificate of three years or less: £819 for the main applicant (Immigration Salary List: £628); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from inside the UK, certificate of three years or less: £943 for the main applicant (Immigration Salary List: £628); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from outside the UK, certificate of three years or less: £819 for each partner or child (Immigration Salary List: £628); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from inside the UK, certificate of three years or less: £943 for each partner or child (Immigration Salary List: £628); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from outside the UK, certificate of over three years: £1,618 for the main applicant (Immigration Salary List: £1,235); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from inside the UK, certificate of over three years: £1,865 for the main applicant (Immigration Salary List: £1,235); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from outside the UK, certificate of over three years: £1,618 for each partner or child (Immigration Salary List: £1,235); one of four alternatives: possible
Visa fee from inside the UK, certificate of over three years: £1,865 for each partner or child (Immigration Salary List: £1,235); one of four alternatives: possible
Immigration health surcharge, £1,035 a year, shown for the 5 years of a five-year certificate (£5,175; the 14 days after it may add half a year): possible
Health surcharge of each partner or child aged 18 or over, £1,035 a year, shown for the 5 years of a five-year certificate (£5,175; the 14 days after it may add half a year): possible
Health surcharge of each child under 18, £776 a year, shown for the 5 years of a five-year certificate (£3,880; the 14 days after it may add half a year): possible

durations.title: Permission until 14 days after the end date of the certificate of sponsorship, which is at most 5 years after its start date
